t: An Andean republic formed in 1830 when Gran Colombia’s Southern District, centred on Quito, Guayaquil and Cuenca, became independent.
Politics long pitted Catholic, conservative Quito against liberal, commercial Guayaquil, from García Moreno to Eloy Alfaro.
Cacao, bananas and then Amazon oil drove its economy; it lost most of its Amazon claim to Peru in 1942 and adopted the dollar in 2000.
dyk: Ecuador’s 2008 constitution was the first in the world to give nature itself enforceable rights, allowing any person to go to court on behalf of a river or forest.
ev: A Quito assembly declares the Southern District of Gran Colombia independent
Gabriel García Moreno is assassinated in Quito
The Liberal Revolution brings Eloy Alfaro to power
The Rio Protocol assigns most of the disputed Amazon to Peru
Oil exports begin through the Trans-Ecuadorian pipeline
Ecuador replaces the sucre with the US dollar
